obligations.condition: A fresh pending credential completes the phone second factor before the transition; its ID token is the session reused by a self-service trigger.

A federated identity linked administratively before the held credential is removed by the session accounts:update deleteProvider. That the provider is absent afterwards and the rest of the account is unchanged are recorded; the held credential's fate afterwards is the observation.
The pending credential held from before the transition is presented to mfaSignIn:start after it; accepted and refused are both valid.
The held credential is finalized on the SMS session opened before the transition; accepted (with token checks recorded as booleans) and refused are both valid.
If the held finalize was accepted, accounts:lookup with the returned ID token names the owner; executed exactly when finalize was accepted.
If the held finalize was accepted, the returned refresh token is redeemed and the derived ID token names the owner; executed exactly when finalize was accepted.
A fresh sign-in with the current password completes the second factor after the run, bounding it against a broken account.

limitations: URLs were read during design; no new frozen full-body source snapshot or completed page-review claim is made by this mapping.

The sources define the operations and the fields; none of them states whether an MFA pending credential issued before this transition remains usable. The observation, not the sources, answers that for the recorded conditions and this trigger only.

One trigger, one owned account, one SMS session, phone MFA with a test phone number, no tenant, no blocking function, one run. For provider-unlink the federated identity is linked administratively as a precondition; a refused link aborts the run and is not an unlink result.

The oracle project's MFA, phone sign-in and SMS region configuration were changed for the run and restored; the restore readback and whole-configuration digest comparison are part of the receipt, not a claim about production defaults.
No execution approval, independent signature verification, SDK checkRevoked, Rules, other triggers, tenants or expiry claim follows from this mapping.
